classification.difficultyReason: Track a point through horizontal dilation, reflection and translation while distinguishing the scope of fractional arguments.

content.prompt: Let $P(-4,y)$ lie on $y=f(x)$. Find the new $x$-coordinate of $P$ on each of the following.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=f\left(-\frac{1}{3}(x-6)\right)\end{align*}$$
Dilate horizontally by factor $3$, reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate right $6$ units. The successive $x$-coordinates are
$$\begin{align*}x_1&=3(-4)=-12\\x_2&=-(-12)=12\\x_3&=12+6=18\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}y&=f\left(-\frac{1}{3}(x-2)\right)\end{align*}$$
Dilate horizontally by factor $3$, reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate right $2$ units. The successive $x$-coordinates are
$$\begin{align*}x_1&=3(-4)=-12\\x_2&=-(-12)=12\\x_3&=12+2=14\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}y&=f\left(-\frac{1}{3}(x+6)\right)\end{align*}$$
Dilate horizontally by factor $3$, reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate left $6$ units. The successive $x$-coordinates are
$$\begin{align*}x_1&=3(-4)=-12\\x_2&=-(-12)=12\\x_3&=12-6=6\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}y&=f\left(-\frac{1}{3}(x+2)\right)\end{align*}$$
Dilate horizontally by factor $3$, reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate left $2$ units. The successive $x$-coordinates are
$$\begin{align*}x_1&=3(-4)=-12\\x_2&=-(-12)=12\\x_3&=12-2=10\end{align*}$$
